newsitem.title: UK: Korean demand lifts Mideast VLCCs, Suezmax firm to.
newsitem.headline: Korean demand lifts Mideast VLCCs, Suezmax firm to.

text.p: Sustained demand for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) from South Korean refiners pushed Middle East freight rates higher on Thursday, brokers said.
Suezmax owners were also benefiting from a surge in fixings on Mediterranean and West African markets, they added.
"It's a booming market for the middle of the month (March). You'd get over W100 now for a million barrels from West Africa to the (United) States," said one.
Yukong and Ssangyong were active again in the market for VLCCs out of the Middle East, paying higher rates for South Korea trips in the second and third decades of March.
On Thursday, Ssangyong fixed the New Wisdom to take 255,000 tonnes from Yanbu to South Korea at W65 loading on March 25.
Brokers said the Korean interest was also lifting rates on other routes. VLCCs to Singapore were able to command around W60 after BP fixed the Nafkratis loading March 10 at W57.5.

Requirements on West African markets were mainly for Suezmax (130,000-tonne) vessels, with the next fixings expected above W100 after Dreyfus took the Kronviken loading March 19 for a U.K. Continent trip at W97.5.
Cross-Mediterranean rates for that class of vessel were also rising, brokers said, catching up with Aframax levels.
ERG fixed the Kinship for a trip from Sidi Kreir to Italy at W110 on March 10, while Arcadia took the Biruinta at W115 from Ceyhan cross Med with U.K./Cont options on March 7.
Inter U.K./Cont rates were little changed to narrowly firmer, aframaxes fixing between W110 and W120 for trips in the first 10 days of March.
